chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Abu Baseer from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) said:

I said to him: The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, 'Retaliation is prescribed for you in the matter of the slain: the free for the free, and the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.'
So he said: The free is not killed for the slave, but he is given a severe beating, and he is fined his value as the blood money (diyah) for the slave.

key_terms.الْحُرُّ: The free person (as opposed to a slave)
key_terms.الْقِصاصُ: Retaliation or retribution in criminal law
key_terms.دِيَةَ: Blood money or compensation paid for killing or injury

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Qisas when a free person kills a slave according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential view on Qisas for a free person killing another's slave, ruling that full blood-for-blood retaliation is not applied; instead, the perpetrator receives a severe beating (darb shadid) and pays the slave's full blood money (diyah). This interpretation highlights the distinct valuation of status in retributive justice, differing from some Sunni schools that may apply full Qisas or adjusted compensation, and underscores the practical application of Quranic verse 2:178 in mixed-status cases.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘The Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:178] O you who believe! The retaliation is Prescribed for you in the matter of the slain, the free for the free, and the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The free would not be killed due to the slave, but he would be whipped with intense whipping, and would be fined his value as wergild for the slave’.
